claims.text: The alloy is an AM-processed dual-nanoprecipitate Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy.
The as-fabricated alloy contains uniformly distributed nanoprecipitates.
High-temperature oxidation induces localized elemental redistribution at nanoprecipitates.
The localized elemental redistribution correlates with formation of protective oxide scales.
In situ APT can reveal localized oxidation-induced elemental redistribution at nanoprecipitates.
Elevated-temperature exposure produces oxygen influx into the alloy.
Incoming oxygen interacts preferentially with nanoprecipitates.
Oxidation produces atomic-scale gradients of alloying elements at nanoprecipitate interfaces.
The interfacial gradients may include enhanced concentrations of Ti, Cr, or Ni.
Elemental redistribution at nanoprecipitate interfaces facilitates protective oxide-scale formation.
APT will detect significant compositional shifts at nanoprecipitate interfaces during early oxide-scale formation.
The predicted nanoscale gradients will be less evident in bulk oxidation measurements.
Conventional isothermal oxidation and SEM/TEM analyses average local chemical variations and do not resolve nanoscale elemental redistribution as proposed for APT.
Findings from this AM-processed alloy may not translate directly to cast or wrought variants.
Findings may not translate directly to HEAs having different nanoprecipitate chemistries.
Sample-preparation or spatial-resolution limitations of in situ APT may impede observation of fine compositional variations.
